summary: Implemented the canonical, versioned, secret-free metadata state record and the real reconciliation/publication path that replaces the task 6.2 DeferredWorkItemProcessor placeholder. MetadataStateEntry is the provider-neutral record (Jellyfin item and library scope, provider/connection scope, typed record/file identity, match classification/fingerprint, normalized metadata snapshot and canonical fingerprint, optional provider version/token, fetch timestamp, explicit MetadataStateKind), with the freshness-window fields recorded but the stale-last-known-good policy left to task 6.5. MetadataStateStore persists it through the existing versioned cache state boundary (StateAuthority.Cache) so a corrupt or semantically invalid entry is discarded and rebuildable and an in-place replacement is one atomic write; MetadataSnapshot/MetadataRecordIdentity are serializable provider-neutral forms so no provider DTO and no polymorphic discriminator enters state. IArrMetadataReader/ArrMetadataReadResult plus the connection-scoped IArrReadClientFactory/ArrReadClientFactory form the provider-neutral read boundary; RadarrMetadataReader/SonarrMetadataReader compose the existing read clients, candidate factories, documented matching order, validated episode-file join, and metadata mappers. MetadataReconciliationProcessor implements IWorkItemProcessor: it re-reads the current configuration snapshot and Jellyfin item, resolves the applicable connection, matches/maps through the reader, computes the canonical fingerprint, re-reads the current configuration and item immediately before publishing, and only then atomically publishes. A changed basis (advanced configuration version, disabled/changed connection, removed/changed/ineligible item) or a provider read failure discards the work without publishing or overwriting metadata state; transient provider failures remain retryable and terminal failures do not. The processor publishes metadata state only and never invokes ArtworkGenerationCoordinator/ArtworkPublisher. DI now registers the store, read-client factory, two provider readers, and the real processor; DeferredWorkItemProcessor is removed and the task 6.1/6.2 queue, worker, coalescing, single-flight, retry, and shutdown behavior is unchanged.

known_limitations: The provider readers do not observe a provider version or revision token, so providerVersion/providerVersionToken are recorded as null; the data model marks both optional and 'if observed', and the canonical metadata/match fingerprints remain the comparison values.
expiresAt/staleUntil are recorded as null and the bounded stale-last-known-good window/outage transitions are intentionally not implemented; that freshness policy is task 6.5.

The processor publishes metadata state only; it does not drive artwork generation/publication or non-terminal artwork-operation recovery (tasks 6.4 and 6.6), so the Phase 5 review MEDIUM lifecycle-fence finding remains open and is not made reachable.

A matched record that disappears between the candidate read and the metadata mapping yields an explicit Unavailable matched-without-metadata entry rather than a re-fetch; the mapper always produces unknown values (not a false claim) for a present record whose file could not be resolved.

The metadata state is non-authoritative cache state and is therefore eligible for the existing cache retention (RenderCacheTtlMinutes/quota) applied by StateRepository.ApplyRetention; eviction is safe because the record is rebuildable, and freshness-specific retention remains task 6.5.

The final basis re-validation and the atomic write are not a single transaction; a configuration replacement in the small window between them is resolved by the next reconciliation. This matches the documented worker behavior (re-read current state immediately before publishing).

The Radarr reader uses the dedicated movie-file endpoint whenever the matched movie reports a current file, adding one provider request per matched movie to obtain full custom-format and media-info fields.
Only in-process validation was performed; no live Jellyfin host or live Arr instance was available, consistent with the pinned-host absence noted for the environment.
